nodes.verbatim_quote: unwounded morphants did not display a defect in fin length or area compared to age matched controls during normal development

strengths: Developmental fin measurements clearly show no defect.
TUNEL staining provides additional evidence against cell death confound.
weaknesses: Developmental data from single experiment in duplicate.
TUNEL at single timepoint only (1 hpw).
required_assumptions: 1 hpw TUNEL is informative about overall cell survival.
evaluation.notes: Adequate controls.

nodes.label: Co-injection of vim MO1 with zebrafish vimentin RNA rescued the regeneration def…
nodes.claim: Co-injection of vim MO1 with zebrafish vimentin RNA rescued the regeneration defect; a second morpholino (MO2) also produced the defect.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Co-injection was sufficient to rescue the regeneration defect observed in the morphants

strengths: RNA rescue is the gold standard for MO validation.
Second MO provides independent confirmation.
Both area and length metrics rescued/confirmed.
weaknesses: Rescue data pooled from two replicates only.
Level of protein restoration not quantified.
required_assumptions: Co-injected RNA produces functional protein.
evaluation.notes: Strong validation of MO specificity.

nodes.label: Time-lapse confocal microscopy showed projections extending from the wound plane…
nodes.claim: Time-lapse confocal microscopy showed projections extending from the wound plane by 24 hpw; unwounded larvae rarely formed projections during development.
nodes.verbatim_quote: The formation of these epithelial extensions, herein referred to as projections, was not present during normal development of the caudal fin, which occurred with the extension of a smooth fin edge.

strengths: Time-lapse imaging directly shows projection formation.
Comparison with developmental fin growth shows distinction.
weaknesses: Developmental comparison is single experiment.
No quantification of projection characteristics.
required_assumptions: Projections are distinct from irregular wound edge morphology.
evaluation.notes: Clear observational evidence.

nodes.label: About 75% of control larvae had visible projections at 24 hpw compared to about …
nodes.claim: About 75% of control larvae had visible projections at 24 hpw compared to about 40% in vim-deficient larvae (p=0.0348; n=3 replicates, ctl 76 larvae total, vim MO 78 larvae total).
nodes.verbatim_quote: more than 75 percent of control larvae had visible projections by 24 hpw while only about 40 percent of vimentin-deficient larvae displayed projections

strengths: Statistically significant (p=0.0348).
Three replicates with reasonable total larvae numbers.
weaknesses: Extremely wide 95% CI for vim MO (7.56-65.78%).
40% of morphants still form projections.
No blinding of scoring described.
Binary scoring is subjective.
alternative_interpretations: High variability could indicate variable MO efficacy rather than a biological graded response.
required_assumptions: Projection scoring is reliable.
Replicate-level statistics are appropriate.
evaluation.notes: Significant but imprecise.

nodes.label: DPI treatment significantly reduced the proportion of larvae forming projections…
nodes.claim: DPI treatment significantly reduced the proportion of larvae forming projections at 24 hpw (p=0.0129; DMSO 72 larvae, DPI 66 larvae over 3 replicates). WA treatment showed similar effects.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Inhibition of early ROS signaling with DPI treatment also significantly reduced the proportion of larvae forming wound healing projections at 24 hpw

strengths: DPI result is significant (p=0.0129).
Three replicates for each treatment.
WA result provides convergent evidence.
weaknesses: DMSO control 95% CI (31.76-99.58%) is absurdly wide, indicating huge inter-replicate variability.
WA data pooled from four replicates but in supplement.
Same subjective scoring issues.
alternative_interpretations: The enormous control variability suggests the assay has poor reproducibility.
required_assumptions: Despite high variability, the treatment effect is real.
evaluation.notes: The very wide CIs in both groups are a concern for reliability.

nodes.label: Bright field and LC-PolScope microscopy revealed organized fibrillar structures …
nodes.claim: Bright field and LC-PolScope microscopy revealed organized fibrillar structures extending into the tips of epithelial projections, with cell membranes stretched outward around the fibers.
nodes.verbatim_quote: We observed thin finger-like projections at the wound edge that extended around fibrillar proteins that protruded into the tips of the projections.

strengths: Multiple complementary imaging modalities (bright field, LC-PolScope, SHG, phalloidin).
Fiber structures clearly visible in the images.
Cell membrane stretching around fibers visible in LC-PolScope images.
weaknesses: Qualitative imaging without quantification.
Static images cannot determine directionality of force.
required_assumptions: The fibrillar structures are collagen.
evaluation.notes: Compelling multi-modal imaging evidence.

nodes.label: SHG imaging combined with phalloidin staining on fixed samples confirmed close a…
nodes.claim: SHG imaging combined with phalloidin staining on fixed samples confirmed close association between fibers and projecting epithelial cells.
nodes.verbatim_quote: This was more clearly shown by dual imaging of SHG fibers and cell borders, using both phalloidin staining on fixed samples

strengths: Dual SHG and phalloidin provides orthogonal validation of fiber-cell association.
Fixed samples allow detailed structural analysis.
weaknesses: Fixation could introduce artifacts.
No quantification of association.
required_assumptions: Fixation preserves the in vivo relationship between fibers and cells.
evaluation.notes: Solid supporting evidence.

nodes.label: Time-lapse multiphoton microscopy of SHG and bright field, and live imaging of S…
nodes.claim: Time-lapse multiphoton microscopy of SHG and bright field, and live imaging of SHG with Tg(krt4:egfp-caax), showed SHG fibers appearing to push epithelial cells outward during wound edge extension.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Live SHG imaging after tail transection confirmed the presence of fibers in the projections and indicated a close association between the fibers and the projecting epithelial cells.

strengths: Live dual imaging provides temporal dynamics of fiber-cell relationship.
Multiple imaging combinations (SHG/bright field and SHG/krt4:egfp-caax).
Time-lapse videos are available for scrutiny.
weaknesses: No quantification of relative extension timing or rates.
Representative examples rather than systematic analysis.
Temporal resolution (~15 min) may not capture which extends first.
The 'pushing' interpretation remains an inference.
alternative_interpretations: Cells could actively extend along fibers rather than being pushed.
Both could be driven by underlying growth.
required_assumptions: The temporal association implies causation (fiber drives cell).
evaluation.notes: Technically impressive but mechanistically ambiguous.

nodes.label: Vim MO reduced wound edge contour length at 24 hpw compared to controls (p=0.000…
nodes.claim: Vim MO reduced wound edge contour length at 24 hpw compared to controls (p=0.0009; ctl n=33, vim MO n=32 over 4 replicates).
nodes.verbatim_quote: There was a decrease in wound contour (reduced fiber extensions) in the vimentin morphants at 24 hpw compared to controls (p=0.0009)

strengths: Good sample sizes (n=33, n=32).
Four replicates.
weaknesses: Contour length is an indirect measure.
Could reflect less overall regrowth.
required_assumptions: Contour length captures fiber projection extent.
evaluation.notes: Well-quantified.

nodes.label: CurveAlign analysis showed a significant decrease in mean fiber angle in vimenti…
nodes.claim: CurveAlign analysis showed a significant decrease in mean fiber angle in vimentin morphants at 24 hpw (p=0.0003; ctl n=30, vim MO n=32), with fibers more parallel to the wound edge.
nodes.verbatim_quote: The fiber angle measurement indicated a significant decrease in orientation, with fibers exhibiting angles more parallel rather than perpendicular, to the wound edge, in the vimentin morphants at 24 hpw (p=0.0003)

strengths: CurveAlign is an established unbiased tool.
Good sample sizes (n=30-32).
Four replicates.
weaknesses: Absolute angle difference is modest (~5-7°).
Causal direction uncertain.
alternative_interpretations: Angle changes could be secondary to reduced regrowth.
required_assumptions: CurveAlign accurately measures fiber angle in SHG images.
The 60-micron analysis window is appropriate.
evaluation.notes: Rigorous quantification with appropriate tools.

nodes.label: qRT-PCR showed reduced col1a1 (p=0.004, n=6 replicates) and col2a1b (p=0.0404, n…
nodes.claim: qRT-PCR showed reduced col1a1 (p=0.004, n=6 replicates) and col2a1b (p=0.0404, n=5 replicates) expression at 24 hpw in vim-deficient larvae versus controls.
nodes.verbatim_quote: vimentin-deficient larvae displayed a reduction in col1a1 and col2a1b expression at 24 hpw compared to controls

strengths: Multiple biological replicates (n=5-6).
Both genes significantly reduced.
Consistent with in vitro data.
weaknesses: Bulk tissue RNA; cell-type resolution lacking.
col2a1b p=0.0404 is marginal.
alternative_interpretations: Fewer fibroblasts rather than reduced per-cell collagen expression.
required_assumptions: Bulk tissue qRT-PCR reflects wound-specific changes.
evaluation.notes: Solid qRT-PCR evidence.

nodes.label: DPI treatment significantly reduced col1a1 (p=0.0464, n=4 replicates) and col2a1…
nodes.claim: DPI treatment significantly reduced col1a1 (p=0.0464, n=4 replicates) and col2a1b (p=0.0126) expression at 24 hpw. DPI and WA also reduced SHG contour length.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Early inhibition of ROS using DPI significantly reduced expression of col1a1 and col2a1b at 24 hpw

strengths: Both collagens reduced by DPI treatment.
WA shows similar effect.
SHG contour also reduced.
weaknesses: col1a1 p=0.0464 is marginal with n=4.
DPI off-target effects.
Cannot distinguish direct ROS effects from vimentin-mediated effects on collagen.
alternative_interpretations: ROS could directly affect collagen-producing cells independent of vimentin.
required_assumptions: DPI effects on collagen are pathway-specific.
evaluation.notes: Consistent with model but not definitive.

nodes.label: Immunofluorescence with anti-type II collagen antibody combined with SHG showed …
nodes.claim: Immunofluorescence with anti-type II collagen antibody combined with SHG showed co-association in unwounded and wounded fins, with strong Col II labeling at broken SHG fiber tips after wounding.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Unwounded fins displayed a highly structured organization exhibiting both SHG and Col II antibody label.

strengths: Dual SHG and immunofluorescence clearly shows co-association.
Both unwounded and wounded conditions examined.
Novel observation of Col II caps at broken fibers.
weaknesses: Only two experiments.
No co-localization quantification.
Col II caps not further investigated.
required_assumptions: Anti-Col II antibody is specific in zebrafish.
evaluation.notes: Clear descriptive evidence.

nodes.label: qRT-PCR showed both col1a1 (p=0.0153, n=6 replicates) and col2a1b (p=0.0294, n=5…
nodes.claim: qRT-PCR showed both col1a1 (p=0.0153, n=6 replicates) and col2a1b (p=0.0294, n=5 replicates) expression increased in wounded fins at 24 hpw.
nodes.verbatim_quote: At 24 hpw, we found an increase in col1a1 and col2a1b expression in the fins of wounded larvae.

strengths: Multiple biological replicates for both genes.
Both significantly increased at 24 hpw.
Appropriate wound-specific tissue collection.
weaknesses: 8 hpw col1a1 trend (p=0.0779) not significant.
8 hpw col2a1b not significant (p=0.9491).
Relatively few replicates for 8 hpw (n=3-5).
required_assumptions: Fin tip collection method consistently captures wound tissue.
evaluation.notes: Good evidence for wound-induced collagen expression at 24 hpw.

nodes.label: Larp6 morpholino knockdown reduced col1a1 but not col2a1b expression, and caused…
nodes.claim: Larp6 morpholino knockdown reduced col1a1 but not col2a1b expression, and caused reduced regenerate area but not length at 3 dpw.
nodes.verbatim_quote: Larp6-deficient larvae have reduced col1a1 expression but no defect in col2a1b expression, consistent with the published in vitro data.

strengths: Selective effect on col1a1 but not col2a1b is consistent with published Larp6 specificity.
Partial phenocopy supports multiple pathway model.
MO validated by RT-PCR.
weaknesses: Single experiment in triplicate for regeneration data.
No rescue experiment.
The area-but-not-length distinction is not mechanistically explained.
alternative_interpretations: Larp6 could affect regeneration through collagen-independent mechanisms.
required_assumptions: Larp6 MO is specific.
Partial phenocopy reflects pathway branching.
evaluation.notes: Interesting but limited replication.

nodes.label: BAPN treatment caused reduced regeneration area and length at 2 dpw, and decreas…
nodes.claim: BAPN treatment caused reduced regeneration area and length at 2 dpw, and decreased SHG fiber mean angle consistent with vimentin-deficient larvae. However, BAPN caused lethality between 4–5 dpf, so toxicity may partly contribute.
nodes.verbatim_quote: It is possible that the observed effects on regeneration were in part due to toxicity but it should be noted that no effect on developmental fin length was observed at the concentration that impaired regeneration.

strengths: BAPN is an established lysyl oxidase inhibitor.
Fiber angle decrease is consistent with vim MO phenotype.
weaknesses: Lethality between 4-5 dpf raises serious toxicity concerns.
Authors acknowledge effects may be 'in part due to toxicity.'
Contour length increased rather than decreased, contradicting the narrative.
Single experiment in triplicate.
BAPN affects all lysyl oxidase substrates, not just collagen.
alternative_interpretations: Toxicity rather than specific collagen effects could drive the regeneration defect.
required_assumptions: BAPN toxicity does not drive the observed regeneration phenotype.
Collagen cross-linking is the primary target at the doses used.
evaluation.notes: The toxicity issue severely undermines this evidence.

nodes.label: SHG imaging showed complete loss of SHG fibers near the wound edge after burn. B…
nodes.claim: SHG imaging showed complete loss of SHG fibers near the wound edge after burn. Burn wounds reduced epithelial projections at 24 hpb versus amputation (p=0.0116; 108 vs 62 larvae over 3 replicates) and reduced healing area (p<0.0001; 65 vs 58 larvae).
nodes.verbatim_quote: Compared to amputated fins, burn wounds resulting in a loss of SHG fiber integrity led to a significant reduction in the percentage of larvae displaying epithelial projections at 24 hpb.

strengths: Clear SHG loss in burn wounds.
Significant reduction in both projections (p=0.0116) and healing area (p<0.0001).
Three replicates with reasonable sample sizes.
weaknesses: Burn wounds cause extensive non-specific tissue damage beyond collagen loss.
Comparing burn to amputation conflates multiple variables.
No rescue experiment (e.g., exogenous collagen) to specifically implicate collagen loss.
alternative_interpretations: Thermal damage to cells, proteins, and vasculature could impair healing independently of collagen loss.
required_assumptions: Collagen fiber loss is the primary cause of impaired healing in burn wounds.
evaluation.notes: The burn experiment is creative but heavily confounded.

nodes.label: Vim+ cells appeared at the burn wound edge but with different morphology compare…
nodes.claim: Vim+ cells appeared at the burn wound edge but with different morphology compared to tail transection.
nodes.verbatim_quote: vim+ cells also appeared at the wound edge in the burn wound, although the morphology of the cells were different compared to tail transection.

strengths: Observed in two experiments.
The different morphology is an interesting observation suggesting wound-type-specific responses.
weaknesses: Purely qualitative observation.
No quantification of cell number or morphological parameters.
The significance of different morphology is unknown.
alternative_interpretations: Different morphology could simply reflect different local tissue architecture in burn vs. transection.
required_assumptions: Cell morphology differences are biologically meaningful.
evaluation.notes: Descriptive observation, not deeply investigated.

summary.overall_assessment: The paper presents 66 claims with mixed overall support (32 high, 5 low).
